parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 HAZOP covers three-phase separator V-001 and associated lines across defined physical parameters (nominal 60 psig and 130 deg F, design range 125 psig to 200 deg F) and startup procedures. The review systematically identifies deviations in pressure, flow, level, temperature, corrosion/erosion, and startup sequencing using only supplied evidence.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Organizational management factors (excluded from classic HAZOP analysis per SYS-09)
Reverse flow from burn pit header to V-001 (unresolved due to absence of flare/burn pit backpressure data in SYS-05)
External fire case relief scenario (unresolved due to lack of plot layout and passive fireproofing information)

consequences: Reduced residence time in V-001 impairing three-phase separation
Liquid carryover into gas line to fuel gas/burn pit
Carryover of free water to Heater-Treater or oil to water treatment

evidence.relevance: Establishes three-phase separation mechanism reliant on density difference and settling time
Lists FIT-101, FAL-103, and SDV-30010 as Node 1 flow and shutdown elements

possible_causes: Failure or excessive opening of upstream flow control valves
recommendations: Verify separation efficiency limits under peak flow conditions
Confirm high-flow alarm and automatic closure logic on SDV-30010 via FIT-101

consequences: Overpressurization of V-001 above nominal 60 psig toward or beyond 125 psig limit
Vessel mechanical stress or potential loss of primary containment

evidence.relevance: Documents nominal pressure of 60 psig and upper limit of 125 psig
Identifies PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, PIT-101, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: PV-101 pressure control loop failure closed
Blockage or restriction in gas outlet to fuel gas system or burn pit
recommendations: Verify sizing and relieving capacity of PSV-101 A/B for full gas blocked outlet scenario
Ensure high-pressure trip logic on PIT-101 initiates isolation via SDV-30010

consequences: Hydrocarbon liquid carryover into gas line resulting in liquid carryover to fuel gas or flaming liquid ejection at burn pit

evidence.relevance: Specifies separated gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Lists level control valves LV-101, LV-102 and isolation valves SDV-101, SDV-102

possible_causes: Downstream line restriction toward Heater-Treater or water treatment
recommendations: Implement independent high-high level trip logic to isolate feed via SDV-30010 upon high level detection

consequences: Loss of liquid seal in V-001
Gas blowby into downstream Heater-Treater or low-pressure water treatment lines causing downstream overpressurization

evidence.relevance: Identifies downstream connection to Heater-Treater separator
Identifies liquid control and safety shut-off valves

possible_causes: LV-101 or LV-102 failing fully open
recommendations: Evaluate gas blowby relief requirements on downstream equipment and verify low-level isolation response of SDV-101 and SDV-102

consequences: Operating temperature rising from nominal 130 deg F toward or exceeding 200 deg F limit
Increased light ends vaporization and accelerated corrosion rate

evidence.relevance: Identifies nominal 130 deg F and 200 deg F operating condition boundary
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger within Node 1

possible_causes: Malfunction or excess heating medium supply in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Confirm high-temperature monitoring and automated heating cutoff on E-001

consequences: Pressure surge, line shock, or abnormal phase distribution through V-001 during start-up sequence

evidence.relevance: Identifies Start/Stop Procedures as an essential study element
Cites procedural error of FWKO start-up without bypass opening

possible_causes: Human procedural error during FWKO start-up: initiating start-up without bypass opening
recommendations: Update standard operating procedures with explicit checklist sign-offs and valve position verification for bypass opening prior to feed introduction

consequences: Wall thinning of V-001 shell and water outlet piping leading to loss of containment

evidence.relevance: Identifies FWKO function in separating free water
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as a required Node 1 study element

possible_causes: Prolonged contact with corrosive separated free water and entrained abrasive solids
recommendations: Implement routine ultrasonic wall-thickness measurement and corrosion monitoring on V-001 boot and water drain piping

uncertainty_notes: Specific setpoints and discharge capacities for PSV-101 A/B are not detailed in the packet.
Interlock logic matrix between PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103, and SDV-30010 is not explicitly defined.
Design pressure and operating limits of downstream equipment (Heater-Treater and water treatment) are unstated.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-HIGHFLOW-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
